fields.acceptance: A testscript lands a change set on a branch, reopens it, applies one more write, lands again, and rhiza check passes; the log holds land, reopen and land entries in order.
fields.statement: rhiza reopen reopens a landed change set whose land is not yet on the base: it appends a reopen entry, the change set is accepted again, takes further writes, and lands again with rhiza land. No log entry is ever deleted.

fields.acceptance: A testscript where the land entry is in the base gets a non-zero exit and that message; one where it is only on the branch succeeds.
fields.statement: Reopening is refused once the change set's land entry is on the base (the merge-base with the default branch's remote, as check uses): landed work on main is final, and the error says so and points to a new change set linked discovered-from.

fields.acceptance: Go tests fold a landed, reopened, relanded change set and check as-is, to-be and the history at each step.
fields.statement: Views treat a reopened change set as accepted until it lands again: as-is leaves it out, to-be and what-if include it, and change show and log show the land, reopen and land history.

fields.acceptance: The format-1 and format-2 corpus pass unchanged, and a new corpus case with a reopen entry reads and renders.
fields.statement: The reopen entry is a new entry type. Format 1 and 2 entries stay byte-identical; if the type needs a new format number, older readers fail with ErrNewerFormat, as carve's did.

fields.acceptance: rhiza guide change-sets (or a topic of its own if change-sets is at its size cap) names rhiza reopen, and the guide tests pass.
fields.statement: The guide tells agents to reopen a change set, never to delete or edit log entries, when they must write after landing on a branch.
